Proposition
[Complex derivative decomposition] 1. 11.1.4\group derivatives Source: thurston:page-0310, thurston:page-0311

On an oriented surface, \[ \partial X= frac 12(\operatorname {div}X)I+ abla ^aX = frac 12\{ (\operatorname {div}X)I+(\operatorname {curl}X)iI\} , \qquad ar\partial X= abla ^{s0}X. \] The operator $\partial X$ is invariant under conformal changes of metric.
Proof

\sketch Any real linear map is the sum of its complex-linear and conjugate- linear parts, and comparison with the trace, antisymmetric, and trace-free components gives the two identities. Using torsion-freeness, $ ar\partial X(Y)= frac 12([Y,X]+i[iY,X])$ removes the metric connection and proves conformal invariance.

□
